clue.text: Head off disaster, having a party with fruit

indicators.note: taking the head off a word means dropping its first letter

parts.note: havoc is widespread disaster or devastation
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone averts catastrophe by throwing a party with a fruit platter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like the verb 'avert', but it removes the first letter of HAVOC, leaving AVOC.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is a pear-shaped tropical fruit with a large stone and green flesh.

clue.text: In grave trouble, certainly in a pickle

indicators.note: trouble suggests the words are disturbed and stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone in serious difficulty is definitely in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickles are preserved in this sour liquid, so it is sure to be found in any pickle.

clue.text: A paper decoration from China

indicators.note: from here signals the letters are made out of the word China, rearranged

explanation.surface: A paper ornament imported from China.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper chain is a loop-linked strip of paper hung as a festive decoration.

clue.text: Drink to give us the shivers?

definitions.meaning: a single swallow or a measure of drink
a cold current of air through a room makes people shiver

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a gulp of liquid and a chilly current of air indoors.

clue.text: They hold the shooters' ammunition before the shelling starts

definitions.text: They hold the shooters' ammunition before the shelling starts

parts.words: They hold the shooters' ammunition before the shelling starts
parts.note: peas fired from pea-shooters sit in their pods until they are shelled from them

explanation.surface: Something stores the gunners' shells ahead of a bombardment.
explanation.walkthrough: The military picture is a disguise: the shooters are pea-shooters and 'shelling' is taking peas out of their cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Pods are the cases that hold peas on the plant until they are shelled.

clue.text: Organ swell may affect one's hearing

parts.note: the ear is an organ of the body
to wax is to grow or swell, as the moon does

explanation.surface: The swelling tones of a church organ may damage your ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A build-up of the waxy secretion in the ear canal can muffle a person's hearing.

clue.text: Apt phrase to describe party wear?

indicators.note: describe in the sense of tracing out a shape signals the letters are drawn into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A fitting expression to sum up what people wear at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured tissue crowns from crackers are worn at Christmas parties and dinners.

clue.text: Attracted by inconclusive result in game, not settled

parts.note: a draw is a game that ends with no winner

indicators.note: settled in the sense of being put in order signals the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Drawn in by a game that ends level and leaves things unresolved.
explanation.walkthrough: A drawn game ends level, with nothing decided, which is the 'inconclusive result'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be drawn to something is to feel pulled towards it, an idiom for being attracted.

clue.text: 16 across that provides glad tidings of rest with happiness

parts.note: comfort is ease or rest
and means together with
joy is great happiness

explanation.surface: A Christmas song bringing good news of ease and gladness.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 across is CAROL; 'God Rest Ye Merry, Gentlemen' sings of 'tidings of comfort and joy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the refrain of a well-known Christmas carol bringing glad news.

clue.text: She takes part in a Victorian nativity play

indicators.note: a name taking part in the words is part of their letters run together

explanation.surface: A girl acts in a nineteenth-century Nativity play.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'VictoriAN NAtivity'. Anna is also the prophetess in Luke's nativity story.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so it can stand for 'she' in the cryptic sense.

clue.text: Happy 16 across turns out to be unauthentic

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters turn over into a new order

parts.note: the answer at 16 across is a Christmas song

explanation.surface: A cheerful Christmas song proves to be a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 across is CAROL, the Christmas song; with HAPPY its letters are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Apocryphal stories are of doubtful authenticity, widely told but probably untrue.

clue.text: Warming drink that takes some beating

definitions.text: Warming drink that takes some beating

parts.words: Warming drink that takes some beating
parts.note: the drink is made with beaten eggs, and 'takes some beating' also means is hard to better

explanation.surface: A hot drink that is hard to improve on.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a Christmas drink of milk, sugar, spirit and whisked eggs.

clue.text: Crying, small boy rejects gift

indicators.note: rejects in the sense of throwing back turns the name round

parts.note: Alf is a short name for a boy called Alfred
a grant is a gift of money

explanation.surface: A tearful little lad turns down a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crying' is meant in its sense of 'crying shame', glaring or outrageous, not weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'a crying need', crying means glaring or blatant, the sense of flagrant.

clue.text: They put a word in when required on stage

definitions.text: They put a word in when required on stage

parts.words: They put a word in when required on stage
parts.note: theatre staff feed forgotten lines to actors during a performance

explanation.surface: People who intervene with a word when a performer needs it.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompters sit off stage and supply actors with lines they have forgotten.

clue.text: A Christmas overhead?

parts.note: a Christmas plant hung above doorways, playing on 'overhead' as a business cost

explanation.surface: A seasonal business expense.
explanation.definitionFit: This parasitic plant is hung up at Christmas so people may kiss beneath it.

clue.text: Girl's name on many people's lips at Christmas

definitions.text: on many people's lips at Christmas
definitions.meaning: a seasonal song sung by many at Christmas

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a female first name and a festive hymn sung in December.

clue.text: Cause embarrassment at a party

parts.note: a bash is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Making someone feel awkward at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash someone is to make them feel ashamed or disconcerted.

clue.text: No deviation from a working party policy?

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for communal work, as in a sewing bee
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: Sticking rigidly to the official position of a political working group.
explanation.walkthrough: BEE is a social gathering for work, chiefly American; the political 'party line' supplies LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A beeline is the straightest route between two points, with no detour at all.

clue.text: Many awakening us with their 28 across

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
arousing someone is waking them from sleep

explanation.surface: A crowd of revellers waking us with their merriment.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 across is REVELRY; 'us with their' only joins the wordplay to that cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Carousing is drinking and making merry noisily in company, the same thing as revelry.

clue.text: Mince pies to include a number of drugs

indicators.note: include means one piece is placed within another
to mince is to chop finely, so the letters are cut up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Chopped pies containing a quantity of narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a number of' reads as a quantity, but the A is the piece placed inside, leaving 'number of drugs' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Opiates are drugs derived from opium, so the word names a group of drugs.

clue.text: Occasion for facing the future with resolution

definitions.text: Occasion for facing the future with resolution

parts.words: Occasion for facing the future with resolution
parts.note: the start of January, when people make resolutions about the year ahead

explanation.surface: A time to face what lies ahead with determination.
explanation.definitionFit: On the first of January many people make resolutions for the coming twelve months.

clue.text: New route right for sightseeing visitors

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A fresh itinerary suitable for tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourer is a car or caravan designed for touring, so it is meant for sightseeing travellers.

clue.text: Touch of viral infection? Shiver!

parts.note: to feel is to touch
a cold is a common viral infection

explanation.surface: Signs of a virus coming on, with shivering.
explanation.definitionFit: Shivering is the body's reaction to sensing a chill, so it shows one is chilled.

clue.text: Marital relations welcomed over Christmas?

parts.note: relatives acquired by marriage who come to stay for the festive season

explanation.surface: A suggestive phrase about married couples at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse's parents and siblings are relations by marriage, often hosted at Christmas.

clue.text: A bell-shaped attachment to the Christmas parcel

indicators.note: shaped means formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tag cut in the shape of a bell, tied on to a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag tied to a parcel naming who it is for is an attachment to it.

clue.text: Tonic water possibly keeps you warm over Christmas

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters might form something else

explanation.surface: A mixer drink somehow keeps you snug through the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy coat worn in the cold months keeps the wearer warm in December.

clue.text: Drink at Sheba's place?

definitions.meaning: a drink brewed from malt and hops
the word placed at the front of 'Sheba' makes the Israeli city Beersheba

explanation.walkthrough: Beersheba is a city in southern Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an alcoholic drink and also the first part of a biblical place name.

clue.text: Noisy celebrations in back bar at the turn of the year

indicators.note: back signals the bar word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise or lift

indicators.note: turn here means the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: YR is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Raucous parties at the bar as the old year ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LEVER into REVEL; 'at the turn of' turns YR into RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelry is lively, noisy merrymaking, as at a celebration.

clue.text: They're to be found in the stable at the inn

definitions.text: They're to be found in the stable at the inn

parts.words: They're to be found in the stable at the inn
parts.note: the men who looked after travellers' horses at old coaching inns

explanation.surface: A nativity image of figures in the stable at the inn.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the nativity scene in Bethlehem, but these are inn grooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostlers were stablemen who looked after the horses of guests at an inn.
